title: Noah and the Bow in the Cloud

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: In Noah's day, the earth had gone bad, Church. Violence everywhere. The Bible says it grieved the LORD in his heart. But one man stood apart. The LORD looked on Noah with favor. Noah walked with God.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God told Noah what was coming. A flood would cover the earth. Noah was to build an ark of gopher wood, a great big boat with rooms inside, sealed with pitch inside and out. He was to bring his wife, his three sons and their wives, and two of every living thing, male and female, with food for all of them.

verses.text: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Thus did Noah; according to all that God commanded him, so did he.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: Picture the work of it. Cutting and fitting and sealing, day after day. Noah did not have a weather report. He had a word from God, and he built on it. He kept building.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When the ark was ready, the animals came two by two, and Noah's family went inside. And then comes one of the tenderest lines in the whole story.

verses.text: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the LORD shut him in.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And they that went in, went in male and female of all flesh, as God had commanded him: and the LORD shut him in.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The LORD shut him in. Noah did not have to pull that great door closed by himself. The rain came forty days and forty nights. The water rose till it covered the mountains. Everything outside the ark was lost. Inside, one family and a boat full of animals rode the water and waited.

verses.text: And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: God remembered Noah. Somebody needs to hear that tonight. A wind passed over the earth, and the water started going down. The ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat. Still Noah waited. He sent out a raven, then a dove. The dove found no place to rest her feet, so she came back to his hand. Seven days later, he sent her out again.

verses.text: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the dove came in to him in the evening; and, lo, in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When I say God is faithful, you say, all the time. God is faithful. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "All the time"] All the time. [PAUSE 3s | screen: "God is faithful"] One olive leaf, and Noah knew.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: One fresh leaf. That is how Noah knew the water was going down. Sometimes the first sign of a new season is small, Church. Do not despise a small leaf.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: When the ground was dry, God brought them all out. Noah built an altar and worshipped. And God made a promise, not just to Noah, but to every living creature.

verses.text: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.

verses.text: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living creature of all flesh; and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.

blocks.speaker: narrator
blocks.text: The old folks used to sing about it, that God gave Noah the rainbow sign. When you see that bow in the cloud after a storm, remember this story. A family kept through the flood. A dove with a leaf. And a God who remembers.
